original.target_description: Primary original study located; exact condition/comparison unresolved among crowd-within accuracy tests.

notes: Identity assessment: canonical text is a complete three-page primary Psychological Science Short Report, Measuring the Crowd Within: Probabilistic Representations Within Individuals, Edward Vul and Harold Pashler, Volume 19, Number 7, pp. 645–647, copyright 2008. Title, authors, journal, year and pagination match the neutral original reference. DOI is not printed and cannot be independently checked within the supplied source. Method, Results, Discussion and references are present. No PDF path supplied. Target: study 1, broad crowd-within description and p. 1 locator do not distinguish condition or comparison. Candidates on p. 645: immediate average versus first guess t(254) = 2.25, p < .05; immediate average versus second guess t(254) = 6.08, p < .01; delayed average versus first guess t(172) = 3.94, with p < .01 continued on p. 646. Further candidates on p. 646: delayed average versus second guess t(172) = 6.59, p < .01; second versus first guess t(254) = 3.6 and t(172) = 2.8, each p < .01; delay difference in averaging benefit t(426) = 2.12, p < .05. These are unassigned candidates. Canonical OCR prints equals signs as 5; evidence preserves that rendering. Method gives 428 recruited participants, with half in each condition; it does not explicitly give final analytic group counts or exclusions. No analytic N inferred from recruitment, assignment proportions or df; no arithmetic performed. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
